turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good morning, Mrs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Turner.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you tell me your full name and your birthday? Odessa Turner.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: April 19, 1935. I'm 91 years old, and I still remember it, so don't you worry.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sharp as ever, did Gloria bring you today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She did. She's out in the waiting room on her phone. She's the one who made me come. Well, I'm glad she did.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What's been going on? I'm just worn out, doctor, for about six weeks now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I nap in the morning and again after lunch, and I used to never nap. My tomatoes are going to waste because I can't get out to the garden.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's a big change for you, any dizziness.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: When I first get up out of bed in the morning, the room kind of swims for a second. Then it passes. Have you fallen at all? No, I hold on to the dresser.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any chest pain or shortness of breath? No chest pain.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I breathe fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Fever, black stools, or losing weight without trying.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you been feeling down or sad?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I'm not sad. Just tired.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's go through your pills. I have amylodipine 5mg once a day for your blood pressure, metaprolol 50mg twice a day, adorvastatin 10 at night, and a baby aspirin 81mg. Anything else? That's right, and I take a Tylenol PM at bedtime because I wasn't sleeping.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Gloria bought me a big bottle about two months ago.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Every night?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every night. Oh, and I quit the vitamin D.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Those pills are too big to swallow.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any other new problems this year?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I had pneumonia last winter, but I got over that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Lungs have been fine since. Good, let me check you. Sitting, your blood pressure is 118 over 64 and your pulse is 52, which is on the slow side. Standing up, the pressure drops to 104 over 60. Your heart is slow but regular, no murmur. Lungs are clear, no swelling in your ankles. Your color looks good, no paleness inside the eyelids. We also did an ECG while you were waiting. It shows a slow, regular rhythm, a rate of 52, and no heart block. so what's making me so tired? I think a big part is your medicines your pulse is slow and the metaprolol may be slowing it too much and the Tylenol PM has difenhydramine in it which is a sleepy antihistamine at 91 it can make you drowsy all day. My goodness I thought it was just the Tylenol. A lot of people think that so here's the plan stop the Tylenol PM if you have aches at night plain Tylenol that's acetaminophen 500 milligrams is fine cut Set the metaprolol down to 25 milligrams twice a day, that's half a tablet. Keep the amylodipine, adorvastatin, and aspirin the same.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What about sleeping then?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Same bedtime every night, no long afternoon naps, and some light in the morning. That helps more than you think. For the vitamin D, I'll switch you to a chewable 1 ,000 units a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A chewable I can do.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I also want some blood work today, a blood count, chemistry panel, thyroid test, and to make sure we're not missing anything else.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Get up slowly, sit on the edge of the bed for a minute first. If you faint, have chest pain, or your pulse gets slower, call us or go to the emergency room. I'll see you in two weeks, and we'll call Gloria at 555 -0177 with the results.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's her number.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you, Doctor.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll bring you some tomatoes if I get my energy back. I'll hold you to that, Mrs. Turner.
